source_file: Berlin 2026 edition for next app devCon 2026 (flutterCon Berlin), sources listed on the page
question: Q4: The Ugly: AI and the Entry-Level Squeeze

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if your company hired a junior, apprentice or working student developer in the last 12 months.
sections.hint: Indeed DE, Sep 2026: entry-level software postings are 70% below 2019 while apprenticeship postings in the field are 27% above. Ask how juniors get in now.
no_hands: Would the path that gave you your first chance still exist today?
For students and juniors: what do you hear back when you apply?
For hirers: did budget, mentoring time, or seniors with AI stop a junior hire?
hands_up: How did you find them: apprenticeship (Ausbildung), dual study, university, career change, community?
What does a junior do on your team now that AI writes the first draft?
Did AI make them productive faster, or let them skip understanding?
follow_ups: If juniors are not hired, where do the seniors come from five years from now?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if code from a coding agent shipped to your production app this year.
sections.hint: JetBrains, Aug 2026: 90% of professional developers use a coding agent at least weekly. Ask who reviewed the code.
no_hands: Where else do you use AI in Flutter work: tests, docs, reviews, planning?
What stops you: policy, trust, cost, or quality?
For team leads: does your team have a written rule for agents?
hands_up: Which Flutter task did the agent get confidently wrong?
Did reviewing the agent's code take longer than writing it yourself?
Did agents change how many people the team needs, or just what they do all day?
Is Flutter easier or harder for agents than Swift or Kotlin?
follow_ups: Which agent habit makes a developer weaker over time?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you let an agent write Swift or Kotlin for you this year.
sections.hint: MobileDev-Bench study, Mar 2026: top AI models fixed 3 to 4% of 407 mobile issues, 5.7% with the right files; no iOS. Ask if it felt safe.
no_hands: Which native task would you hand to an agent first?
Who writes the Swift or Kotlin on your project today?
For the seniors: does cheap agent-written native code make Flutter more or less attractive?
hands_up: What did it write: a platform channel, a plugin, a whole native module?
How did you check the Swift or Kotlin before it shipped?
Did it make you more likely to go native next time, or less?
follow_ups: If agents make native cheap, what is the remaining argument for one codebase?
Where do you draw the line on shipping code you could not have written?

wrap_up: In a world where agents write the first draft, what should a Flutter developer become excellent at?
What would you tell a student who asks whether to start in mobile at all?
